title: Introduce Special Case

solutions.title: One patient record that already knows how to answer
solutions.tradeoff: Every board function shrinks to a one-line field read, but the two factories that build a Patient now carry the weight those nine checks used to share - a real cost when a tenth board line is added later and has to be taught to both factories instead of appended to a nine-item list.

reviewFocus: Count the id === "unknown" (or similarly-shaped) comparisons left anywhere in the solution's src-facing functions. It should be zero - every one of the nine has to move into a factory, not just be tidied in place.

Does isBillable in src/ actually disagree with the solution for an unidentified patient? If a stray fix crept in while un-refactoring, the whole reason tests-fixed/ exists disappears and the exercise stops proving anything.
Does tests/ ever call isBillable(unknownPatient()) directly? It must not - that is the one call the shared suite cannot pin, and it belongs only in tests-fixed/.

Is UNKNOWN_PATIENT (or its equivalent) a single shared value, or does something rebuild an equivalent object on every call? A fresh object every time isn't wrong, but the walkthrough should say which was chosen and why.

Registered patients with no insurance on file and the unidentified patient both start from a null-ish signal - does the solution still tell 'self-pay' and 'not yet identified' apart, or did the special case collapse them into one label?
